evidence: The issue proposes a proactive extension conflict/compatibility warning system. None of the candidates describe the same underlying bug: they concern workspace-scoped extension toggling, tracing the source of AI customization objects, CLI install-target disambiguation across forks, AI task completion notifications, or extension update cache invalidation.

Both describe model-specific reasoningEffort settings in chatLanguageModels.json being keyed too broadly, so changing effort for one model/provider overwrites an existing entry instead of creating a separate scoped one. Candidate 325069 explicitly mentions collisions/overwrites when switching reasoningEffort between providers with the same model id.

The issue is about double-clicking a word/line causing the Ask Questions widget to dismiss. None of the candidates describe this specific widget-closing behavior; they involve text selection inside the widget, tab selection, search-box selection, browser Cmd+A, or tool JSON display.

The issue is about Agents window failing to re-detect an existing PR after a repo-scoped GitHub token becomes stale and returns 401. The candidates are about unrelated auth/sign-in failures, remote file-reading behavior, ADO re-fetch dedup, or GHE Copilot auth support, none of which describe PR detection with a stale repo token.

Both report the same underlying bug in VS Code's Help menu: the 'Help | Report Issue' option is missing/broken, and the template mentions it. Candidate #325032 explicitly reproduces via Help | Report Issue and discusses the broken reporting flow.

Candidate #325589 describes the same kind of flicker in the chat UI tied to resizing/main panel width: "Flickering of text under chat input on resize of main editor window." The others are different UI elements (scrollbar, placeholder, update button, inline terminal).

Both issues describe PowerShell/tree-sitter parsing failures preventing terminal auto-approval for commands with `--`. Candidate #325635 specifically mentions `npm exec -- ...` in PowerShell, matching one of the exact parse-trigger cases and the same underlying grammar limitation.

The issue is a specific flaky unit test in CopilotAgent _resumeSession fallback timing out after a Start Over truncate leaves the session empty. The candidates are about different tests/suites and failures (Agents Window smoke session timeout, request cancellation timing, generic flaky unit test, Copilot SDK customization flakiness, and a Windows heap corruption crash). None describe the same underlying bug.
Candidate issues are about cross-file cursor prediction or MultiDiffEditorWidget disposed service guards, which are unrelated to indent guides rendering and null visible range in prepareRender.
All entries have identical title and identical sparse body ('Copilot Completion Feedback' with blank completion text), indicating the same underlying issue.

The issue only shows a generic Python/Pyright undefined-variable ignore note, while the candidates are about VS Code problems like missing local problem detection, unused variable coloring, assertion failures, and tokenizer errors. No candidate describes the same underlying bug.

The issue is about intermittent mocha timeouts in specific AgentHost node I/O tests, fixed by raising test timeouts. None of the candidates describe the same timeout-at-2000ms build failure or the same test suites.

Candidate #323094 specifically covers the same AGENTS.md discovery scan and same flag pattern, making it the closest underlying bug match.

The issue is about missing padding between the remote indicator and the restricted mode indicator. None of the candidates mention this specific indicator-to-indicator spacing; they focus on tab padding, sidebar overlap, icon-button gaps, extensions list padding, or detail panel spacing.

The issue is specific to launching VS Code via Code.exe on Windows and missing environment values, while the candidates are about unrelated problems: frozen dialogs, profile switching, terminal input/state, or GDB debugging errors.
The issue text is too unclear/garbled to identify a specific underlying bug, and none of the candidates describe the same concrete problem with enough detail to confirm a duplicate.

Both issues are about the PR failed-CI icon being unclear. The candidate specifically requests a PR icon with a failure indication for CI errors, matching the complaint that the failed CI icon is confusing and has poor contrast.

The issue is about CS50.dev terminal/run-file integration missing, while the candidates describe unrelated problems such as codespace loading, submission failure, connection setup, install issues, or terminal restart/shortcut inconsistencies. No same underlying bug is evident.
